panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: T1 MRI transverse image from a patient with vulvar melanoma; in-text describes a vulvar mass on pelvic MRI. B: T2 MRI transverse image from a patient with vulvar melanoma; in-text describes a vulvar mass on pelvic MRI. C: T1 MRI longitudinal image from a patient with vulvar melanoma; in-text describes a vulvar mass on pelvic MRI. D: Ultrasound image captioned as vulvar melanoma in the patient; the specific ultrasound mass finding is not in the provided vocabulary, so it is proposed. E: Doppler image captioned as enriched blood flow in vulvar melanoma; no exact vocabulary finding is available, so the vascularity finding is proposed. F: Gross surgical specimen captioned as vulvar melanoma; the specimen shows a nodular tumor mass consistent with the vocabulary finding of a nodular vulvar mass.

in_text_mentions: Enhanced pelvic MRI (Fig. 1A–C) demonstrated a vulvar mass involving labia and corpus cavernosum, the urethra and the lower part of the vagina; enlarged lymph nodes were detected in the bilateral groin area, left external iliac vessels, and abdominal aorta; multiple small lymph nodes were also detected in the bilateral external iliac vessels and obturator area; while multiple nodules and flaky shadows had been recorded in the pelvic bones, lumbosacral vertebrae, and bilateral femurs, considering bone metastases. Duration surgery, a tumor tissue with a diameter of 3 cm was removed, and the Breslow thickness was estimated as 1 cm (Fig. 1F). The post-surgical histological analysis revealed invasion of the dermal reticular layer (Clark grade IV), and involvement of the urethra and the right medial cutaneous margin of the vulva, without vulvar flap involvement. No further chemotherapy or radiotherapy had been applied for this patient, and the patient has been living for two years after surgery, as follow-up confirmed.
